provider_query: 过去 48 小时内关于半导体出口管制的一条新闻
answer:
过去约 48 小时内，最明确的一条是路透社独家：SK 海力士把在美国建厂，与获准向中国大连厂出口更多美国芯片设备挂钩。

**主新闻（2026-10-14/15）**  
SK 海力士正寻求美国批准，向其中国大连 NAND 厂出口更多美国产设备（用于闲置产能扩产），并把此作为在美国新建 NAND 工厂的条件。消息人士称，Solidigm（SK 海力士美国子公司）尚未获准 2027 年更多设备与技术出口；公司表示相关设备安装正与美国政府协商并在授权下进行。背景是美国限制向中国出口芯片制造设备，以延缓其先进半导体（含 AI 与军事用途）发展，同时推动外资在美建厂。  
来源：Reuters（Karen Freifeld、Hyunjoo Jin），2026-10-15  
https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/sk-hynix-conditions-new-us-factory-more-us-chip-equipment-exports-china-sources-2026-10-15/

results.title: Why this little known Chinese chipmaker has caused a global stock rout - CNBC
results.snippet: Tech stocks plummeted on Tuesday after a Chinese memory chipmaker said it had made significant progress in developing new and more efficient designs. ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT, announced over the weekend it had made headway on new architecture which will increase memory density by packing more data into a smaller space. The announcement spooked the market because CXMT is China's leading rival to global memory makers including Micron, SK Hynix and Samsung. One of the biggest questions for CXMT after its IPO was whether it would be able to narrow the capability gap with Micron, Samsung and SK Hynix, particularly in high-bandwidth memory — a key component of AI chip systems. While huge domestic demand is supporting CXMT, it still faces challenges accessing chipmaking equipment, which has been effectively barred from China by U.S. export controls, including ASML's extreme ultraviolet, or EUV, lithography machines, which are needed to manufacture the most advanced semiconductors.

results.title: Chinese tech firm charged with smuggling ‘dual-use’ products out of country - South China Morning Post
results.snippet: # China charges tech firm with smuggling restricted ‘dual-use’ optical lenses out of country. As Beijing tightens export controls on strategic technologies, the case highlights risk of criminal prosecution for companies. Chinese authorities have charged a Shenzhen-listed firm and its chairman over smuggling restricted “dual-use” optical lenses out of the country, in a case that lawyers said underscores the growing risk of criminal prosecution for export control violations as Beijing tightens restrictions on strategic materials and technologies. Prosecutors in Shanghai alleged that the company and the individuals exported controlled optical lenses without obtaining the required export licences for dual-use items, which can serve both civilian and military purposes, between August 2023 and April 2025. The case underscores the compliance risks facing Chinese manufacturers as Beijing expands export controls of dual-use items and the materials used to make them amid intensifying tech rivalry with the US.

results.title: US probes Foxconn, Luxshare and 18 others over AI server power patents - The Next Web
results.snippet: AUS trade body has opened a patent case against 20 companies over the power systems inside AI servers. Foxconn, Luxshare and Quanta are among them.The US International Trade Commission acted after a complaint by power-chip maker Vicor, it said on Friday. The case covers systems that feed power to top-end chips from directly below them, and the computers that use them. Besides Foxconn, Luxshare and Quanta, the companies named include Delta Electronics, Monolithic Power Systems, Infineon, Flex and Celestica. Vicor wants the products barred from the US, and the firms ordered to stop selling them. Apple supplier Luxshare said in a filing on Saturday that it does not expect the probe to have a material impact on its production, operations or results, Bloomberg reported. The products are still being tested by customers and are not in mass production, Luxshare said. The commission has not ruled on the claims yet. The commission will set a target date to finish the case within 45 days.

results.title: The most important alliances will lead to critical minerals - Defense One
results.snippet: ## In the 21st century, geopolitical and economic advantage will depend on forging new links in strong supply chains. The U.S. administration’s concerns about supply-chain vulnerabilities are shared with some of America’s closest allies, with the leaders of the G7 striking an urgent tone in the joint declaration on securing supply chains for critical minerals coming out of their June summit in Évian-les-Bains: “In light of the high degree of market concentration, the need to reduce vulnerabilities regarding those resources and the growing use of arbitrary trade restrictions, we recall the urgency of diversifying our supply chains and building our collective resilience.” Moreover, in a marked departure from the past G7 communiqués on the subject which tended to be long on platitudes and short on substance, the group committed to specific quantifiable targets for reducing its members’ dependence on the unnamed “single supplier outside the G7 and partner countries” whose “use of non-market policies and practices and economic coercion, including arbitrary export restrictions and retaliatory measures on critical minerals and their related dual-use items” threaten the security of G7 to less than 60 percent by 2030 for REEs and permanent magnets and thereafter to half “as soon as possible.”.
